first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4%, and memory_86 directly indicates that shorter onboarding improved completion, time-to-value, and early adoption. Promotional pricing addresses the competitive threat, but memory_73 reports materially worse 30-day retention, creating a clear risk to sustainable qualified revenue. Verify both the strongest directly relevant intervention and the most plausible competing option before committing.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment to shorten onboarding. The verified source directly addresses the current 4% completion decline and previously delivered +13% completion, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and +3% 30-day retention, aligning with sustainable qualified revenue. Do not choose promotional pricing despite competitive pressure: its +18% qualified-revenue lift was paired with a verified 12% retention decline and failure through the first renewal cycle. A controlled experiment preserves uncertainty about whether the prior onboarding effect will replicate under current conditions.

final2.rationale: Proceed with the shortened-onboarding experiment. The verified evidence shows gains in completion (+13%), time-to-value (-2.1 days), and 30-day retention (+3%), directly addressing current onboarding and activation weakness while supporting sustainable revenue. The competitor’s deeper price cut raises urgency but does not reverse the verified downside of promotional pricing: although it lifted qualified revenue 18% initially, retention fell 12% and the cohort failed through renewal. Avoid an unverified reactive discount strategy and test the durable lever under current market conditions.
